description.narrative: Det övergripande målet för CID/BUKA är att tillhandahålla snabb och korrekt rapportering i allmänhetens intresse och med en aktivistisk hållning samt hålla de offentliga tjänstemännen ansvariga. CID/BUKA är ett gott exempel för journalistkåren med målet att tillhandahålla höga etiska standarder i rapporteringen. CID/BUKA samarbetar med likasinnade civilsamhällesorganisationer och rapporterar om åtgärder som vidtagits av medborgaraktivister och därigenom främjar dem. CID/BUKA ökar också medvetenheten om sociala frågor och genom att utöva prövade och lösningsbaserad journalistik.

The overall objective of the CID/BUKA is to provide timely and accurate reporting in the public interest and with an activist stance, as well as to hold public officials accountable. CID/BUKA sets a good example for the journalistic profession with the aim of providing high ethical standards in reporting. CID/BUKA cooperates with like-minded civil society organisations and reports on actions taken by civic activists and thereby promotes them. CID/BUKA also raises awareness of social issues and by practising tried and tested and solution-based journalism

-Be placed in the top 3 of most followed and trusted media in the Western Balkans region
-Increase the production of journalistic content
-Increase commercial revenue
-Establish additional newsrooms

description.narrative:
The Core Activities Bridging Phase (2024-2025) implemented by the / BUKA contributed to maintaining independent public-interest journalism in Bosnia and Herzegovina during a period marked by increasing political pressure on media, restrictive legislative initiatives, and financial uncertainty for independent outlets. The project focused on sustaining editorial production, strengthening digital platforms, and improving the organizational sustainability of the BUKA media outlet.
During the reporting period, BUKA maintained a high level of editorial output and expanded its digital reach across multiple platforms. The organization produced a large number of articles, podcasts, interviews, and multimedia reports addressing governance, corruption, EU integration, human rights, and environmental issues. Audience engagement increased significantly, with the outlet reporting more than 41 million web page visits, 352 million Facebook views, and strong growth across Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok, particularly among younger audiences.
A key operational milestone was the launch of a new Content Management System (CMS) in August 2024, which improved website performance, analytics, and search engine visibility, resulting in increased user sessions and direct traffic. The organization also expanded multimedia production and strengthened cross-platform storytelling through podcasts, short-form video, and social media engagement strategies. In parallel, CID/BUKA implemented focusing on digital analytics, SEO optimization, and social media production. The capacity building of staff resulted in improved technical skills in digital marketing, analytics, multimedia production, and data-driven editorial planning, which contributed to stronger audience engagement and more efficient newsroom operations. In addition, training in financial management and compliance strengthened internal governance, transparency, and the organisations ability to meet donor requirements. Overall, these efforts enhanced CID/BUKAs organisational resilience and its ability to adapt to a challenging media environment.
CID/BUKA strengthened its institutional sustainability by improving internal governance structures and enhancing financial management and compliance systems. This included better financial reporting, stronger internal coordination, and more robust administrative procedures to increase accountability and transparency. In parallel, staff received targeted training in financial compliance, including anti-money laundering (AML) standards and donor reporting requirements, which contributed to more effective internal controls.While the report does not explicitly mention the adoption of new formal internal guidelines, the introduction of improved financial procedures, compliance training, and strengthened management systems suggests that internal operational practices were further formalised to support compliance and institutional sustainability.
